To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multiplex reverse transcription PCR (mRT-PC) assay was developed and applied to detect H5 and H 9 subtypes of AIV and NDV in one reaction.
the developed mRT-PCR assay is highly sensitive and specific for the detection of H5-AVI, H9-AVI and NDV, and may be used as an effective method for the diagnosis of these pathogens.
a multiplex reverse transcription PCR assay was developed for rapid and specific discrimination between H5 and H 9 subtypes of AIV and NDV in one reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of AIV and NDV in the poultry industry and the development of mRT-PCRs for the rapid and accurate diagnosis of AIV and Newcastle disease.
a rapid, simple and specific method for the simultaneous detection and discrimination of H5-AV, H9-AV and NDV in a single reaction.
the development and evaluation of an mRT-PCR assay for the rapid and sensitive detection of H5 and 9 subtypes of AIV and NDV.

this assay could be used as a rapid, specific and sensitive diagnostic tool for detection of H5 and/or H9 AIV and NDV in poultry.
the mRT-PCR assay developed in this study is a reliable and sensitive method for rapid detection of H5 and/or H9 subtypes AIV and NDV in poultry.
this mRT-PCR assay could be a rapid and specific method to discriminate the three pathogens.

the mRT-PCR assay could be a useful tool for the rapid detection and discrimination of H5- and H9-subtypes of AIV and NDV.
